Latest release: v3.5.0

Your Claude and Codex limits, always in view.

A small macOS menu bar app that shows how much of your 5-hour and weekly limits you have used, and when they reset.

Download v3.5.0 View on GitHub

Free and open source · macOS 13 or later · Intel and Apple silicon

Made to be read at a glance

One look at the menu bar tells you where you stand.

Know whether you are on pace

The pace graph plots each limit against the time that has passed in its window. The dotted diagonal is an even rate: above it you are using faster than the clock, below it you have room to spare. Weekly limits can count weekdays only. Prefer a simple ring? Switch any time.

A shape for every limit

Each limit has its own shape, and its color deepens as usage climbs. Show a percentage, an icon, or both, in the size that suits your menu bar.

Everything else you would expect

  • Every Claude app, one quota

    claude.ai, Claude Code, the desktop and mobile apps and Cowork all draw from the same limits. The menu bar shows the total.

  • Codex, if you use it

    Add a Codex account to follow Codex CLI, the IDE extension and Codex web next to Claude. Without one, Codex never shows up.

  • Alerts at your thresholds

    A macOS notification when usage crosses the levels you choose, and another when a limit resets.

  • Refresh that adapts

    Checks often while usage is moving and slows down when it is idle, so the numbers stay current without flooding the servers.

  • Several accounts

    Sign in through your browser with Google, SSO or a passkey. Add Claude and Codex accounts, name them, and switch from the menu bar.

  • Seven languages

    English, Japanese, Korean, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, French and German. It follows your system language, or pick one.

Your data stays on your Mac

No account with us, no server of ours, nothing to phone home to.

  • No analytics

    The app only talks to Claude and Codex, to GitHub to check for updates, and to codex-reset.com for the optional Codex reset announcement.

  • Credentials in the Keychain

    Session keys and tokens are kept in the macOS Keychain, never in plain text, and usage responses are never cached to disk.

  • Sandboxed

    It runs inside the macOS App Sandbox with only the access it needs to sign in, fetch usage and install updates.

  • Open source

    Every line is on GitHub under the MIT license, open for anyone to read and audit.

Get Usage4Claude

macOS 13 Ventura or later, on Intel or Apple silicon.

Download v3.5.0

  1. Install

    Open the downloaded .dmg and drag Usage4Claude into Applications.

  2. Allow the first launch

    The app is not notarized by Apple, so macOS asks once. On macOS 15 or later, open it, click Done, then choose Open Anyway in System Settings → Privacy & Security. On macOS 14 or earlier, Control-click the app and choose Open.

  3. Sign in

    Sign in to Claude or Codex in your browser. When the Keychain asks for access, choose Always Allow.

Works with Claude Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise; Free plans have no usage data to read. New versions install from inside the app.
